validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all clear. The Wick Meter Station Expansion Project is a real, FERC-certificated facility on Rover Pipeline's Sherwood Lateral in Tyler County, West Virginia -- confirmed by TWO genuinely independent government sources that do not trace to each other or to GEM: (1) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' sheet, which carries a dedicated row for 'Wick Meter Station Project' (Pipeline Operator Name: Rover Pipeline; Status: Completed; Completed Date 2020-07-15; State(s) WV/WV; Cost $4.9M; Additional Capacity 300 MMcf/d; Docket CP20-10; Notes: 'Takeaway capacity out of Marcellus; new interconnection with Equitrans system'); and (2) three separate Federal Register notices in FERC Docket CP20-10-000 -- the Jan 21, 2020 Notice of Intent to Prepare an EA (published Jan 28, 2020), the Jan 24, 2020 Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review (published Jan 30, 2020), and a further 2024 Notice of Application (Docket CP24-504-000, published Aug 14, 2024, re: downsizing the same station -- see the separate spec caveat below). The Jan 30, 2020 notice's own Project Description confirms the CORRECT classification: 'an ultrasonic meter skid and other ancillary facilities... piping and valves, electronic flow measurement devices, flow conditioners, instrumentation, telemetry, gas analysis devices, gas quality monitoring devices, flow control valves, condensate storage tank' on about 2.1 acres -- i.e. a discrete meter/regulator station, with NO new mainline pipe. This positively confirms (not merely fails to contradict) that LengthKnown=0/Diameter=blank is CORRECT for this row, per the standing 'expansion with no new physical pipe' rule -- it is a real difference of scope from the other three Rover rows, not a state error. The irregular=true flag on the Location cluster (StartState==EndState=West Virginia) is likewise explained and justified by this being a single-site facility, not a linear segment. NOT A DUPLICATE: this is one of four GEM rows for the Rover system (P0392 'Phase 1', P2438 'Phase 2', P2604 'Rover Expansion', and this row) which a sibling researcher (P2438.json, same batch) confirmed are additive, non-overlapping stages of one project (1700 + 1550 + 175 MMcf/d = 3.425 Bcf/d current total capacity, matching boereport.com's April 2026 reporting) -- this row's 300 MMcf/d Wick facility is a distinct receipt-point expansion (new Eureka Midstream gathering interconnect) layered on top of that total, not a re-statement of any of the other three rows' capacity, and no other roster row describes a Tyler County meter/regulator station.

validity.recommendation: update Owner2 from 'Blackstone' to 'Ares Management' (32.4% stake); Owner1 (Energy Transfer, 32.57%) and Owner3 (Traverse, 35.00%) are unaffected and remain accurate
validity.researcher_notes: Same finding a sibling researcher already staged against P2438 (Rover Phase 2), applied here since it affects all four Rover Pipeline rows. GEM's current Owner2='Blackstone' (32.44%) is STALE: on April 29, 2026, Ares Management (via its Infrastructure Opportunities strategy) acquired Blackstone Energy Transition Partners' entire 32.4% stake in Rover Pipeline -- confirmed independently by Blackstone's own press release (blackstone.com), Pipeline & Gas Journal (pgjonline.com), and BOE Report (boereport.com), all dated late April 2026 and all naming 'Rover Pipeline' and the 32.4% figure (matching GEM's 32.44%). Owner1 (Energy Transfer) and Owner3 (Traverse) are not implicated by this transaction. Separately, I independently corroborated the ORIGINAL 2017 formation of this ownership structure (before the 2026 Ares swap) via Energy Transfer Partners, L.P.'s FY2017 Form 10-K (SEC EDGAR, accession 0001161154-18-000018): the 10-K discloses that in October 2017 ETP contributed a 49.9% interest in 'Rover Holdco' (the entity that owns 65% of Rover Pipeline) to a Blackstone-managed fund, leaving Rover Holdco owned 50.1% ETP / 49.9% Blackstone; the same 10-K's consolidation table separately lists ETP's own effective interest in 'Rover Pipeline' as 32.6%. The arithmetic ties out exactly to GEM's recorded percentages: 50.1% x 65% = 32.57% (matches Owner1's 32.57% precisely) and 49.9% x 65% = 32.44% (matches the disputed Owner2's percentage exactly, confirming only the ENTITY NAME changed in 2026, not the 32.44% stake size); the remaining 35% (100% - 65% held via Holdco) is consistent with Owner3 Traverse's 35.00% direct interest. I did not find a second, fully independent (non-Energy Transfer-family) source stating the exact 32.57%/32.44% breakdown -- Energy Transfer Equity, L.P.'s own contemporaneous 10-K discusses the same transaction but is the same corporate family (one origin, not a second independent source) -- so I'm citing the ETP 10-K at medium tier for the historical percentage math, while relying on the 3 independent 2026 press/trade sources (high tier) for the current Owner2 name correction, which is the actionable finding here.

I could not determine from Federal Register (no further notices found after Aug 2024) or from EIA's current/planned-projects sheet (no matching row for a Wick downsize) whether Docket CP24-504-000 has since been approved or completed. If it has been approved/completed since GEM's LastUpdated (2023-08-05), Capacity would need to change from 300.00 to 100.00 MMcf/d at the next sweep. Recommend a future researcher re-check FERC Docket CP24-504-000 (elibrary.ferc.gov) or a fresh EIA workbook pull before the next annual update to see if this has resolved.
